reader.requirement: At --std 85 FUNCTION ORD must return the ordinal position (lowest 1) of its one-character class alphabetic or alphanumeric argument in the program collating sequence: the native sequence when no PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE is named, else the named alphabet's order, including THRU ranges, ALSO equivalences and the unlisted characters following in native order.

edition-consulted.switches: ArgPredicate.AppliesAt: ORD's CharacterCategory predicate is Since 2002, so at 85 a one-position numeric-edited item (class alphanumeric in 1985) is admitted; at 2023 it is refused

reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no for the returned value: p6ord prints the same 13 lines at 85 and 2023. The argument screen differs (numeric-edited admitted only at 85), which is AR1, not this rule.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf03_08 covers a literal-list alphabet; THRU ranges, ALSO equivalences, LOW-VALUE/HIGH-VALUE, space and characters after the listed block, the native sequence and reference-modified arguments are covered by these probes.

probes.printed: ALPHABET AL IS "Z" THRU "X" "a" ALSO "A" ALSO "b" "0": Z=1 Y=2 X=3 a=4 A=4 b=4 0=5 SP=38 B=70 LOW=1 HIGH=65534
probes.expected: Z..X at 1-3, the ALSO group shares 4, 0 is 5; unlisted characters follow in native order from 6, so space (32 native predecessors) is 38 and B (66 predecessors less 0 and A) is 70; LOW-VALUE is position 1 and HIGH-VALUE the last position of the 65,536-character native set less the 7 listed characters, 65534
code unit + 1 over the documented 65,536-unit native set (docs/conformance/7/DOC-A.1-8.md)

probes.printed: COBOL1627: FUNCTION ORD argument-1 is 2 character position(s) in length

probes.expected: the same ordinal at both editions

citations.check: OK  §1989:A.2.31.4 RV1  (2.31.4 Returned Values)  the text is in RV1

reader.notes: Without a program collating sequence ORD is code unit + 1. With one, the binder flags the call and the renderer passes the __COLLATE weights, whose Weight reader places ALSO members on one position and unlisted characters after the listed block in native order. Every probed position matches the 1985 alphabet rules.
